5 × 10-5 kg water/ (m2 kPa s), the length of membrane tube (in m) is______.

questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 3.65 to 3.75.

opening of 4.75 mm; whereas, 80% of the ground product passes through 0.5 mm
opening. If the power required to grind 2 tonnes/h of the feed material is

questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 6.25 to 6.32.

questions.questionText:

options: Difference in the cloud cover between the land and the sea.
Difference in the albedo between the land and the sea.

Difference in the surface roughness between the land and the sea.

The directions of the South Pacific Subtropical Gyre and the North Atlantic
Subtropical Gyre are __________ and _________, respectively.
questions.explanation: The official answer key provided by IIT Roorkee is Option (B).

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:

questions.explanation: The official answer key provided by IIT Roorkee is Option (C).

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
Accumulated rainfall is often measured in mm. If the density of rain water is 1000
kg m-3 then, one mm of rain is equal to ________________ kg m-2 of rain. (in
integer).
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 1 to 1.

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
Acceleration due to Coriolis force of a water parcel at a location P (67 °E, 20 °N)
moving with a speed of 0.35 m s-1 is _______________ × 10-5 m s-2. (Round off to
two decimal places)
[Assume the angular velocity of the Earth is 7.3 × 10-5 s-1.]
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 1.72 to 1.78.

questions.questionText:

geostrophic currents within the isolines?
questions.explanation: The official answer key provided by IIT Roorkee is Option (C).

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
One kg of dry air at 15 °C is isothermally compressed to one-tenth of its initial
volume. The work done on the system is _________________ kJ. (Round off to the
nearest integer.)
[Assume that the gas constant for dry air is 287 × 105 J K-1 kg-1.]
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 189 to 191.

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
In hot weather, a human body cools by the evaporation of sweat from its skin. The
amount of water that must evaporate to cool the body by 1 C is ____________ %
of the body mass. (Round off to two decimal places.)
[Assume that latent heat of vaporization of water is 2.25 × 106 J kg-1 and specific
heat capacities of both human body and liquid water is 4.2 × 103 J K-1 kg-1.]
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 0.18 to 0.19.

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
A floating hot air balloon with volume 1000 m3 and gross mass (excluding the air
in the balloon) 100 kg is in hydrostatic balance where the external air temperature
is 10 °C and density is 1 kg m-3. The temperature of the air inside the balloon is
_______________ °C. (Round off to the nearest integer.)
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 40 to 42.

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
The solar constant for the Earth is 1368 W m-2. Consider the planet Jupiter whose
mass is 320 times that of the Earth and distance from the Sun is 5.2 times that of the
Earth. The solar constant for Jupiter is _____________ W m-2. (Round off to the
nearest integer.)
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 50 to 52.

questions.sectionName: Section H: Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
questions.questionText:
A column of air mass extending from surface to a height of 10 km moving eastward
along 30 °N strikes a north-south oriented mountain range. While crossing the
mountain range, the air mass acquires a relative vorticity of −3.65 × 10-5 s-1 at the
top. If the air mass maintains the same latitude and conserves potential vorticity, the
height of the mountain range is _______ km. (Round off to the nearest integer.)
[Assume the angular velocity of the Earth is 7.3 × 10-5 s-1 and initial relative
vorticity is zero.]
questions.explanation: The official accepted numerical range provided by IIT Roorkee is 5 to 5.
